The appellant has filed the present second application under Section 430 read with Section 528 BNSS, 2023 (erstwhile Sections 389/482 Cr.P.C.) seeking suspension of sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the appeal.

The appellant also prays for exemption from filing certified/translated/typed copies of annexures, stating he has been in judicial custody for about 3 years and 11 months and belongs to a poor stratum of society.
He submits that the certified copy of Annexure A1 (Order dated 25.09.2024) is not readily available and undertakes to file the same as directed by this Court.

2. By way of the present appeal, the appellant assails the judgment of conviction dated 22.11.2023 and order on sentence dated 27.03.2024 passed by the learned ASJ (SC-POCSO), South District,
Saket Courts, New Delhi in SC No. 7823/2016 arising out of FIR No. 1404/2016 registered under

The appellant was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years with a fine of Rs.10,000/-, and in default, to further undergo simple imprisonment for 30 days for the offence punishable under Section 376(1) IPC.
Benefit under Section 428 Cr.P.C. was granted to the appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant has, inter alia, contended that the complainant/victim statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and her deposition before the Trial Court contain material contradictions on core aspects of the prosecution case.

It is urged that the medical evidence is inconsistent, inasmuch as (PW-1) Dr. Mrinalini Gupta initially deposed that there could be no cause for hymenal rupture other than forceful sexual assault on an unmarried girl, but later admitted in cross-examination that such rupture could occur due to multiple other reasons.
Reliance is also placed on the testimony of (PW-11) Dr. Pooja Singh in another criminal case involving the same prosecutrix, where her hymen was found intact.

It is further submitted that the appellant was on bail during the trial for over five years without any misuse of liberty, has already undergone a substantial part of his sentence, and maintains good conduct in custody.

4. Learned APP for the State has opposed the applications and drawn attention to the testimony of the victim (PW-2) and her mother (PW-7), asserting that their accounts, read together, establish the offence beyond reasonable doubt.
It is submitted that the Trial Court, upon a detailed appreciation of the evidence, found the prosecution version trustworthy and consistent, and no case for suspension of sentence is made out 5.
A perusal of the Trial Court record shows that the victim (PW-2) gave a detailed account of the incident and identified the appellant as the This is a digitally signed order.

The prosecution case is supported by the testimony of her mother (PW-7) and other witnesses examined during trial.
6.

Looking into the fact that the appellant's application seeking suspension of sentence was dismissed on 25.09.2024 and as per the nominal roll dated 04.08.2025, the appellant has undergone only about 3 years, 10 months and 02 days with remission earned 3 months and 28 days and an unexpired portion of sentence of 5 years 10 months.
I find no ground to entertain the present applications at this stage.
Accordingly, the same are dismissed.
List in due course.
